extracted.intended_audience: startup founders and PR/communications teams at startups (tech/startup product launches)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and distributing a product-launch press release aimed at technology/startup audiences, covering headline, structure, length, content focus, distribution and startup-specific messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 100 characters; strong action verbs; avoid vague buzzwords ("game-changing"); 10-20 words ideal length; include specific value proposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: BAD: "Company X Launches New Software" — GOOD: "Company X Unveils AI-Powered Software That Cuts Design Time in Half". Emphasize specific value rather than generic launch language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 1: Concise Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: What the product is; who can benefit; main value proposition; market need addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place product name and core value proposition immediately — readers/journalists should grasp the announcement in seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 2: Specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Key features; how it works; differentiation from competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, specific feature descriptions (avoid generic claims) and explain how the product functions and stands apart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 3: CEO Quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic context; why this product, why now; vision for impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote should add authority and context rather than sounding promotional — explain strategy and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 4: Industry Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Market trends; why announcement is timely; how it fits broader landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the product within market dynamics to create a news hook and relevance for reporters and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 5: Customer/User Quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer perspective; early use cases; specific benefits realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real customer language and specific outcomes strengthen credibility; can be a second leadership quote if customer quotes aren't available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 6: Boilerplate + Contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Company history; current scope; press contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise boilerplate about the company and clear media contact information (name, email, phone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.description: 300-500 words traditional; 600-800 for major launches; one page maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases concise — journalists scan quickly. Use longer length only for very major announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Value, Not Features
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why now" angle critical; measurable impact; customer problem solved; specific use cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the value and impact to the customer; avoid listing features without explaining the problem solved or measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution for Tech/Startup PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists receive 100+ pitches/week and spend less than 10 seconds scanning; paste full content in email body (no attachments); find reporters who cover your space; tailor each email to journalist's beat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize targeted, personalized pitches and make it easy for reporters to read the full release immediately in the body of the email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup-Specific Advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize innovation; differentiation; growth potential; how product challenges status quo; founder story if compelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the narrative to highlight startup strengths (innovation, vision, growth) and incorporate founder story only when it adds news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product clearly named and described
rubrics_metrics.description: The product must be named and clearly described in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the first paragraph identifies the product and succinctly explains what it is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value proposition stated in first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: State the product's value proposition in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the 'why it matters' explicit up front so busy journalists immediately see the relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific features (not generic claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific features rather than generic, vague claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid buzzwords; provide concrete examples of functionality and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer problem addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the customer problem the product solves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link product features to real customer pain points and use cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation from competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the product differs from competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight unique capabilities, approach, technology, or go-to-market distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market context provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide market context and trends to situate the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data or trend language to show why the launch is timely and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative quotes (not promotional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes that add authority and context rather than promotional fluff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should explain strategy, impact, or customer benefit in a credible voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing/availability included
rubrics_metrics.description: Include pricing and availability information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State when the product is available and at what price (or how to access pricing/demo/beta) so journalists can report practical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear next steps for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear next steps (e.g., how to get a demo, arrange interviews, obtain assets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for reporters to follow up by offering demos, beta access, or scheduling information.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-resolution product images provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide high-resolution product images for press use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to hi-res images to facilitate coverage; ensure image captions/credits are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beta access or demos offered to press
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer beta access or demos to the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving reporters hands-on access increases likelihood of coverage and depth of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-relevant news hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a news hook that ties the product to an industry-relevant event/trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong hook (timing, trend, data point) makes the announcement more newsworthy to beat reporters.
